evidence: The original presetIsCustomized returned `(presetRootOps[name]?.length ?? 0) > 0` while the reviewer cites replay's `ops.length === 0 -> continue` after decode-filtering, so an all-malformed log reads customized over an unchanged tree; the fix decodes with the same decodeLayoutOp.
guidance_note: When a diagnostic summarizes what a replay step does, derive it from the same decode/filter the replay runs instead of from the raw input count.

evidence: The agent itself confirms reset actions contribute nothing to deriveConfigActionValidators, so an emptied preset's banner click fails reset-config's membership check; it registered the key in config-validators instead of the reviewer's options, but the landed scope (presets an action targets) is narrower than reply 1's plan (every declared preset), and the ab536a4 banner comment still says 'every declared preset UNCONDITIONALLY'.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that justifies a new action as 'no new gate needed', trace the gate's derivation function to confirm which action kinds actually register keys.

evidence: The preset-name check was `name === '' || name.includes('/')` and escapeTemplateLiteral only escapes backslash and quote, so a newline-bearing name reached a Go-template literal; rejecting newlines at load mirrors groupLabelSpec, and the name is also an identifier on other seams.
guidance_note: When splicing a user-supplied name into synthesized template source, check the name validator against every character the template grammar forbids, as the existing group-label path already did.

evidence: F2's fix (25f6485) added presetRootOpsContributions with its own `presets.${name}.rootOps` spelling beside edit-chrome.ts's, creating the second unshared builder the reviewer names; ab536a4 shows presetRootOpsKey extracted and both sites importing it.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a second site that formats a key another module already formats, extract the builder in the same commit rather than re-spelling it.

evidence: The doc still said 'currently has a non-empty op log' after F1's fix made presetIsCustomized decode-based; the agent's own reply says 'the round-1 fix ... changed the definition but I left the doc describing the old ... wording'.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a function's definition, grep the docs for prose describing that function's contract and update it in the same commit.

evidence: ident() collapses non-alphanumerics to '_' and synthesized artifacts are keyed by `edit.${presetIdent}.*` in a plain object, so 'quick-look' and 'quick_look' overwrite each other; that keying predates review, so this is not fix-caused. The load-time rejection was the reviewer's first option.
guidance_note: When keying synthesized artifacts by a lossy transform of user names, add an injectivity check over the transformed set at the point where the full set is known.

evidence: The round-0 summary already called the unsanitized cross-project presetRootOps throw pre-existing; presetByName throws for undeclared names and the overrides file is machine-global, so sanitizing like sanitizePersistedPresetOverride (ab536a4) is the matching fix.
guidance_note: When building a new feature on persisted state from a shared, machine-global file, check that every field of it is sanitized against the current project the way its sibling fields are.

evidence: F2's fix made presetRootOpsContributions depend on parsePersistTarget, whose PRESET_ROOT_OPS_KEY `([^.]+)` cannot match a legal dotted preset name, so the emptied-preset reset orphan F2 closed comes back for dotted names; ed33bc3's greedy `(.+)` regex fixes the round trip.
guidance_note: When a fix routes keys through an existing parser, round-trip every legal input of the domain (here, every name the preset validator accepts) through builder then parser in a test.

evidence: F6's fix (ab536a4) put presetIdentCollisions in validatePresets, which runs per source before mergeWithDefault, while synthesis keys by ident on the merged config; the reviewer concedes no bundled name collides today, but the guard sat on the wrong set. ed33bc3 moved it to cross-ref on cfg.presets.
guidance_note: Place a guard on the same data the hazard it protects consumes: before choosing a validation pass, find where the synthesis that keys by ident actually runs, which here is on the merged config.

evidence: False-positive flag: escapeTemplateLiteral and the banner splice predate review (round-0 F3 quotes them), and ab536a4 does not touch them. No test sent a quote or backslash preset name through compile and render, and the ed33bc3 test adds that coverage.
guidance_note: When a fix chooses 'reject some characters, escape the rest', add a test for the escaped class through the real compile path alongside the rejection test.

evidence: Same root as F8: presetRootOpsKey (F4's fix) is called 'the inverse of PRESET_ROOT_OPS_KEY's parse', but `[^.]+` rejects 'presets.v1.compact.rootOps', which breaks F2's presetRootOpsContributions for dotted names. The agent took the reviewer's second option (greedy capture), which round-trips because the suffix is anchored.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a builder and a parser are inverses, assert the claim with a property test over the validator's accepted domain before shipping it.

evidence: False-positive flag: prependCustomizedBanner's ungated outer wrapper existed in round 0 (F2's hunk) and ab536a4 only changed its comment. A root-level `when` is legal and the new outer container dropped it, so the banner leaked past the author's gate.
guidance_note: When wrapping an author's node in a new synthesized container, carry every gating attribute of the wrapped node onto the wrapper.

evidence: False-positive flag: check's hardcoded `presetCustomized: false` was in the original PR (the round-0 summary discusses it). It conflicts with checkPayload's stated rich-fixture design, so `.preset.customized`-gated content was never rendered by check.
guidance_note: When adding a new input var to a render payload, check how the static checker's fixture drives it and add a pass if the fixture can never make it true.

evidence: F5's fix rewrote the doc to 'at least one op it can still decode and replay' (ab536a4 diff), but presetIsCustomized checks decode only, while replay skips stale-target ops. Softening the doc was the reviewer's second option, and the O(tree) cost argument is a fair carrying-cost trade.
guidance_note: When rewording a doc to match code, write only what the code checks; 'decode' and 'replay' are different predicates.

evidence: F6's fix (ab536a4) introduced a private ident() copy in loader/presets.ts with a comment calling the duplication justified, and F9's fix (ed33bc3) moved that copy into cross-ref.ts. The guard's correctness depends on matching edit-chrome's ident with no shared definition, so the drift risk is real.
guidance_note: When a guard exists only to enforce another module's transform, import that transform rather than reimplementing it, even if it is one line.

evidence: ed33bc3 adds `...(splicedRoot.when !== undefined && { when: splicedRoot.when })`, which only fires when the preset root is a container. A bare-segment root gets wrapped by spliceEditChromeForPreset in a synthetic container without its `when`, so the leak F12 described survives for that shape.
guidance_note: When fixing a gate carry-up on one node shape, enumerate every LayoutNode kind a root can be and trace each through the wrapping path.

evidence: ed33bc3's second whole-tree render concatenates `[...primary.segmentErrors, ...customizedCheck.segmentErrors.map(...)]`, so an unconditional segment error that check used to report once is now reported twice, with a misleading customized-gate tag.
guidance_note: When adding a second full pass whose results are merged with the first, run an existing failing fixture through both passes and check the merged count.

evidence: Duplicate of F17 with a concrete repro: the pre-existing ungated `chip` fixture now yields '2 segment errors' after ed33bc3. The same dedup-by-segment fix in dabdd11 resolves both.
guidance_note: When adding a second full pass whose results are merged with the first, run an existing failing fixture through both passes and check the merged count.

evidence: False-positive flag: ed33bc3's doc diff only rewrote the prose paragraph, not the check:pass snippet. The snippet writes presets.compact.rootOps but never makes compact active, so `.preset.customized` (read for the effective preset, which is 'default') stays false.
guidance_note: When writing a doc example that narrates cause and effect, check that the example's state actually reaches the narrated effect, since check:pass only proves it loads.

narrative: 10 of 19 findings exist because of an earlier fix. They include doc drift from the decode-based customized check (F1 to F5 to F14), F2's registration fix relying on a parser that could not round-trip dotted preset names (F8, F11), the ident-collision guard placed per source and duplicated (F9, F15), a `when` carry-up that missed bare-segment roots (F16), and a second check pass that double-reported errors (F17, F18). Every later round also had at least one finding on pre-review code, so no round was purely avoidable. The fixes kept widening the surface: each fix added a new seam that the next round probed. F2's fix also left an unflagged drifted comment in prependCustomizedBanner claiming registration for 'every declared preset UNCONDITIONALLY'.
guidance_observations: Fixes were pushed within minutes of each round with only targeted tests. A round-trip or enumeration test over each new seam (builder/parser, root node kinds, merged pass output) would have pre-empted most fix-caused findings.
Doc prose describing a function's contract was edited twice in reaction to reviews (F5, F14) instead of being re-derived from the code each time it changed.
Reply plans sometimes diverged from what landed (F2: every declared preset in the plan, targeted presets in the code) without the drifted code comment being updated.

evidence: The diff replaces a SHA-pinned action with `brandon-fryslie/coding-agent-review@v1` and passes DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, deleting the comment that explained the pin. Reverting restored the pin, so the regression is gone from this repo. 'Can't verify the SHA from here' is weak, though: a tag's SHA is resolvable with git ls-remote.
guidance_note: Before committing installer output that changes a credential-bearing workflow, diff it against the previous version for removed pins and route a template regression to the template's repo as a ticket in the same session.

evidence: The reviewer itself says the file may be regenerated template output ('unverifiable here'), and the agent's F1 reply calls it 'the agent-code-review-setup uptake this PR pulled in', which suggests installer output, not a hand edit. Reverting a generator's write leaves the template emitting the same workflow on the next run, and no ticket against the template repo is visible.
guidance_note: When a generated file's new output is wrong, fix the generating template (or file a ticket on its repo) and regenerate, rather than reverting the rendered file, which the next installer run overwrites.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 that also names `actions/checkout@v6`, which the diff unpinned from d23441a. The revert restored both pins.
Duplicate of F1, adding that the job holds write permissions. The revert to the SHA-pinned workflow addresses it.
The new comment implied only `fg` may be a template. The round-1 summary confirms bg and fg both go through resolveSegmentColors and accept templates, and the fixed comment says so.
guidance_note: When rewriting a comment for one field of a pair, check whether the new capability it describes applies to both fields.

evidence: The deleted comment said 'BOTH credentials are passed on purpose' and the prior workflow passed CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. That contradicts the new claim that the token is never provisioned, and the revert removed both the false comment and the PROVIDER pin.
guidance_note: When a new comment justifies removing something, check it against the comment it replaces; here the deleted text directly contradicted the new rationale.

narrative: A small demo fix carried an incidental rewrite of the generated code-review workflow. That rewrite unpinned a credential-bearing action and dropped a secret, which drew four S5/S2 security findings and one stale-rationale finding. The agent reverted the whole workflow change instead of fixing it, which cleared the findings in one round. If that file was installer output, the generating template still emits the same bad workflow, and the thread shows no ticket filed against it.
guidance_observations: Changes to an unrelated generated CI file rode along in a demo-fix PR. Reviewing generator output for security regressions before committing would have avoided the round.
The agent called the fix 'belongs in the template repo' but left no visible ticket there, so the template defect has no owner.

evidence: synthesizeSettingsMenu ensures edit.toggle whenever canHostSessionState holds, which satisfies edit chrome's demand gate for nearly every config, while the docs and the edit-mode.ts header still said 'demand-driven ... a config that never references edit.toggle gets none of this'. The agent reconciled all three sites.
guidance_note: When a new feature makes an opt-in path effectively always-on, grep for every doc and header comment that promises the opt-in behavior and update them in the same PR.

evidence: The agent confirms ownValidators was residue from an earlier revision and that test/ sits outside lint with noUnusedLocals false, so nothing caught it.
guidance_note: When replacing an assertion helper in a test file, remove its import in the same edit, since test/ has no unused-import lint.

evidence: The doc said 'present in every bar, whatever the config says', but synthesis returns the config untouched without session.id. The agent added the precondition and paired it with F4's load error.
guidance_note: When documenting a guarantee, read the synthesizing function's early-return conditions and state them as preconditions.

evidence: The agent reproduced it: a config with no session.id that places 'settings.menu' loads clean, then the un-lowered reference throws in lookupSegment at render. Gating the cross-ref bypass on the same exported canHostSessionState predicate removes the divergence.
guidance_note: When a validator exempts a name because a later pass will provide it, make the exemption read the same predicate the providing pass uses.

evidence: The test helper re-spelled 'settings.' and 'edit.' while SETTINGS_NS and EDIT_NS are exported. A rename would silently stop filtering, so importing the constants is correct.
guidance_note: When a test helper filters by a production namespace, import the namespace constant rather than writing the literal.

evidence: `key === 'preset'` blacklists a bare key that fixtures such as dsl-persist-actions legitimately write. The reviewer's APPLY_PRESET_ACTION comparison does not fit because validator entries are keyed by state key, so deriving authorship from the config's own actions is a sound alternative.
guidance_note: When a filter must exclude synthesized entries that share a name users can also write, discriminate by provenance, not by the bare string.

evidence: The agent showed edit chrome's insert affordance calls menuStateKey with `edit.<preset>.insertSeg.<n>` and ident() collapses the dots, then ran the derivation and got 30+ `menus.edit_default_insertSeg_*` keys. F13's reviewer later agreed the branch is 'NOT vestigial'.
guidance_note: When a filter arm matches keys produced indirectly, comment the producer at the arm so its liveness is visible without re-deriving it.

evidence: The agent's probe showed the menu gated by an author's '{{ .flag }}' on a first row. The plan to make no gated node a host was revised when the bare-segment-root banner test failed, and what landed (descend only into ungated children, honor a root gate) matches the reviewer's first option, with the revision explained on the thread.
guidance_note: When placing a must-always-exist node by default, check every ancestor on its path for an author `when` and treat gated inner rows as non-hosts.

evidence: The substring filter missed `menus.settings_presets...`, so the agent switched to decoding URLs via effectsOf. It declined filtering bare 'preset' because ownLinks has no config to check authorship and dsl-persist-actions declares `persist: 'preset'`, so over-filtering would go silent; that is a sound split.
guidance_note: When filtering wire-encoded URLs, decode them with the same decoder the daemon uses instead of matching substrings.

evidence: The literal re-spelling of PRESET_CUSTOMIZED_VAR was real and was fixed by exporting the constant. The derive-from-config suggestion has no discriminator: after synthesis the merged config holds one 'preset.customized' entry whether ensured or authored, so declining that half is right.
guidance_note: When a test helper names a production constant, export and import it the first time rather than copying the string.

evidence: projectDir comes from mkdtempSync, while removeTmpDirs only cleans prepareIsolatedDaemonEnv's directories. The sibling e2e test rmSyncs its projectDir, so the new test was leaking a temp dir each run.
guidance_note: When writing a new e2e test modeled on a sibling, diff its setup/teardown against the sibling's so every resource created gets cleaned up.

evidence:
insertSegmentFrom holds addableDomainName = `edit.addable.

`, so `!d.startsWith(SETTINGS_NS)` could never fail. The agent asserted on addableSegmentDomains values with a non-empty guard and mutation-checked it (1 failed with a leak injected, 23 passed without).
guidance_note: Mutation-check every new negative assertion by injecting the violation it guards against before trusting it.

evidence: F9's fix (abbde7b) rebuilt ownLinks with its own `k.startsWith(EDIT_NS)` test instead of reusing isReservedChromeKey, so it missed the `menus.edit_` prefix the agent had just defended as live in F7. 2ab651b switches to the shared predicate.
guidance_note: When rewriting one of two sibling filters, reuse the sibling's predicate instead of writing a parallel prefix list, especially right after defending an arm of it on another thread.

evidence: Flag false positive: 2ab651b only rewired ownLinks to isReservedChromeKey and does not contain the `startsWith('presets.') && endsWith('.rootOps')` arm, and the packet does not show when that arm was added. Using parsePersistTarget is the canonical read-side authority and also handles dotted names correctly.
guidance_note: When a test helper matches a production key format, call the production parser for that format rather than hand-rolling a prefix/suffix match.

evidence: Flag false positive: 2ab651b touches only ambient-chrome.ts and settings-menu.test.ts. In the original PR, pickerConfig's root was isolated but menuRowConfig's bare h root was not, so appendAnchor put the toggle in row 0. The agent confirmed by mutation that the isolation is load-bearing (6 failed when reverted).
guidance_note: When isolating ambient chrome in one fixture of a suite, sweep every fixture in the same file that declares session.id and apply the same isolation.

narrative: This large feature PR drew mostly genuine first-sight findings on pre-review code: doc contradictions, the cross-ref anchor bypass, gated-first-row anchor inheritance, a vacuous test, a temp-dir leak. The agent verified claims by running probes and mutation checks. It pushed back correctly once (F7), and on F9 and F10 it split the suggestions and declined the half that would have caused silent over-filtering. The one fix-caused finding is F13: F9's rewrite of ownLinks wrote a parallel prefix test instead of reusing isReservedChromeKey. Both flagged round-4 findings are on code the flagged commit did not change.
guidance_observations: Probe-and-mutate verification of reviewer claims (F7 key dump, F12 and F15 mutation runs) settled disputes with evidence instead of argument.

The test-helper filter went through four review rounds (F5, F6, F9, F10, F13, F14), which suggests designing it once around decoded keys and the production predicates instead of growing it per finding.
